display_name: The whole Holidays Act 2003 (NZ) under one top-level goal — for a holiday or leave event, is the employee entitled, how much must the employer pay, when, and is an alternative holiday earned — and six goals: pay measures, annual holidays, public holidays, sick and bereavement leave, family violence leave, enforcement and records

scope: Every provision of the Act as in the PCO's version as at 20 December 2023 (ss 1-91, Schedule 1AA, Schedules 1-3), from the text converted from the PCO XML. Inputs: who is an employee or involved (ERA ss 6, 142W); whether a day would otherwise be a working day (s 12), except where the calendar reads it from the usual weekdays; what the employee would have received on a day, and gross earnings over a period; Matariki Observance Day and the local anniversary day; agreements and Labour Inspector determinations; the s 63(1)(b) hours test date; the days left in the sick and family violence entitlements. Carried as text: the provisions listed in `provisions carried as text`. Refused: conduct before 1 April 2016 (penalties, s 77A), family violence leave before 1 April 2019, sick leave in a 12-month period beginning before 24 July 2021, and the public-holiday calendar before 2022.

not_reviewed.note: No domain expert has read this against the Act. An independent test pass was run on 2026-10-15 (tests-independent.l4, 298 assertions from expectations written before the encoding was read). It found one error — s 40(3) pay for an employee not yet entitled — now fixed, and two gaps — s 16(3) in the cash-up and closedown rates, and a cash-up not limited to the entitlement — now closed. 3 assertions still fail by design: the author counted 14 days' notice by date difference, the encoding in clear days (fork F4). The converted text lacks paragraph labels and the formula symbols of ss 8(2) and 9A(2). The pipeline has not been run. On 2026-10-17, at the user's direction, Legislation Act 2019 s 55 was applied to the deadline for allowing annual holidays (s 18) and for commencing penalty actions (s 76); 3 independent assertion(s) written before that change now fail by design.

forks.F2: s 9A: average daily pay where relevant daily pay cannot be determined; otherwise only if daily pay varies and the employer chooses it.
forks.F3: s 16(2)(a)(vi): other unpaid leave over 1 week is left out whole.
forks.F4: ss 19(2), 32(3), 57(3): 14 days' notice means 14 clear days.
forks.F5: s 16(1)-(2): uncounted unpaid leave defers the anniversary by its length.
forks.F6: ss 18(1), 61(2), 76(5): within 12 months after a date ends on its first anniversary.
forks.F7: s 22(2)(b)(ii): 12 months' work is counted to the end of the last pay period before the holiday.
forks.F8: ss 23, 25, 34: deductions above the 8% leave 0 owed, not a debt.
forks.F9: s 33(3): the part of a closedown beyond an entitled employee's entitlement, without agreement, is unpaid under this Act.
forks.F10: s 44(2): holidays moved by ss 45, 45A onto the same day count once.
forks.F11: s 66: 10 days plus up to 10 carried over, at most 20.
forks.F12: s 40(3): paid at the daily pay for the last day of employment, and only for an employee entitled to annual holidays.
forks.S55: Legislation Act 2019 s 55 (applied 2026-10-17 at the user's direction): the deadline for allowing annual holidays (s 18) and for commencing penalty actions (s 76) run to the next working day (Legislation Act s 13, with the Matariki dates in Schedule 1 of the Te Kāhui o Matariki Public Holiday Act 2022) when they end on a non-working day.
